source_text:
Ἄρ' οὖν ἐταμιεύου καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει τῷ κτησαμένῳ συνεῖναι, μηδὲ τὸ λεγόμενον ὀνόματι πρᾶγμα χρᾶναι βουληθείς, ἑαυτῷ δὲ φυσικὸν ἐκδικῆσαι νόμον,
ἐπειράθης ὑπερβολῇ σωφροσύνης ἀσκούμενος. 73 Ῥουβὴν καὶ Ἰούδας ἄριστα συνεβουλευσάτην, ἄλλως μέντοι, πρὸς ἄνδρας γὰρ εἶχον ἀνημέρους.
thought_title: Joseph's pure conscience and natural law
orientation: Eustathius continues addressing Joseph directly, asking whether he kept his conscience pure toward his master and defended a natural law in himself, then contrasts this with the advice of Reuben and Judah.
pass_a_gloss: So then, were you keeping in store, with a pure conscience, to be with the one who had acquired you, not even wishing to defile the thing said in name as a matter, but to defend a natural law for yourself, you were tested, being trained in an excess of self-control. Reuben and Judah gave the best advice, though in a different way, for they were dealing with savage men.

choices.why: The verb ταμιεύω means to store up or keep as a treasurer; the middle voice suggests Joseph was preserving something within himself, so a literal rendering keeps the sense of guarded reserve.

choices.english: the one who had acquired you
choices.why: The aorist participle of κτάομαι means one who has acquired or gained possession; this preserves the master-slave relationship without importing 'master' where the source uses a participle.

choices.english: the thing said in name as a matter
choices.why: The phrase is deliberately awkward in Greek, contrasting a mere name with an actual thing; the literal rendering keeps that tension.
ἐκδικέω means to avenge or vindicate; in this context Joseph is vindicating or defending the natural law in himself, so 'defend' captures the active stance.
The dual form συνεβουλευσάτην indicates two people (Reuben and Judah) acting together; 'gave the best advice' preserves the superlative force of ἄριστα.
ἀνήμερος means untamed or wild, applied to men; 'savage' captures the moral wildness of the Shechemites in context.

pass_b_english: So were you managing to keep a pure conscience toward the one who had acquired you, not even willing to perform the deed so called by name, and choosing instead to defend the natural law in yourself? You were tested while practicing an extreme of self-control. Reuben and Judah gave the best advice—but it was different, for they were dealing with savage men.

problems.quote: refusing even to defile the thing that was called by name a matter
problems.source_quote: μηδὲ τὸ λεγόμενον ὀνόματι πρᾶγμα χρᾶναι βουληθείς
problems.why: "χρᾶναι" means to use/consummate, not defile; "λεγόμενον ὀνόματι πρᾶγμα" is the deed so-called by name, i.e. sexual intercourse.
problems.fix: refusing even to perform the deed so called by name
problems.ruling: χρᾶναι means 'to use,' not 'defile'; λεγόμενον ὀνόματι πράγμα = 'the deed called by name,' i.e. sexual intercourse.

problems.quote: keeping a pure conscience in store for
problems.source_quote: ἐταμιεύου καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει τῷ κτησαμένῳ συνεῖναι
problems.why: "ἐταμιεύου" with infinitive means managing/refraining; "συνεῖναι" is to associate with, not in store for.
problems.fix: did you manage to keep a pure conscience in associating with your master
problems.ruling: ἐταμίευο with συνεῖναι infinitive = 'to keep/preserve for association with'; 'in store for' mistranslates the construction.

problems.quote: You were tested by an extreme of self-control
problems.why: "ἀσκούμενος" is middle participle (training/practicing), not passive; Joseph actively practiced self-control.
problems.fix: you were tested while practicing an extreme of self-control
problems.ruling: ἀσκούμενος is middle 'practicing/training oneself,' not passive 'tested'; Joseph actively practiced self-control.

problems.quote: though in a different way, since they were dealing with savage men
problems.source_quote: ἄλλως μέντοι, πρὸς ἄνδρας γὰρ εἶχον ἀνημέρους
problems.why: "ἄλλως" means otherwise/unsuccessfully, not "in a different way"; their advice failed because the men were savage.
problems.fix: but unsuccessfully, for they were dealing with savage men
problems.ruling: ἄλλως here means 'otherwise/unsuccessfully,' not 'in a different way'; their advice failed because men were savage.

edits.old: keeping a pure conscience in store for the one who had acquired you
edits.new: managing to keep a pure conscience in associating with the one who had acquired you

edits.old: refusing even to defile the thing that was called by name a matter
edits.new: refusing even to perform the deed so called by name

edits.old: You were tested by an extreme of self-control
edits.new: You were tested while practicing an extreme of self-control

edits.old: though in a different way, since they were dealing with savage men
edits.new: but unsuccessfully, for they were dealing with savage men

fixed: Fixed 'keeping a pure conscience in store for' to 'managing to keep a pure conscience in associating with'.
Fixed 'refusing even to defile the thing that was called by name a matter' to 'refusing even to perform the deed so called by name'.
Fixed 'You were tested by an extreme of self-control' to 'You were tested while practicing an extreme of self-control'.
Fixed 'though in a different way, since they were dealing with savage men' to 'but unsuccessfully, for they were dealing with savage men'.

problems.why: Glossary requires 'conscience' for συνείδησις, but 'associating' misses the sexual sense of συνεῖναι here (cohabiting/be with).
problems.fix: So were you managing to keep a pure conscience toward the one who had acquired you, refusing even to perform the deed so called by name, choosing instead to defend the natural law in yourself?
problems.ruling: συνεῖναι in context of σωφροσύνη and sexual temptation means 'have intercourse'; 'associating' loses euphemistic sexual sense.

problems.why: ἄλλως μέντοι means 'but otherwise/in a different way' or 'but it was different,' not 'unsuccessfully'—the point is their advice was excellent but the situation was different (they faced savage men), not that they failed.
problems.fix: but it was different, for they were dealing with savage men
problems.ruling: ἄλλως μέντοι means 'but otherwise/differently'; 'unsuccessfully' wrongly imports failure, misleading reader about Reuben and Judah's counsel.

edits.old: managing to keep a pure conscience in associating with the one who had acquired you
edits.new: managing to keep a pure conscience toward the one who had acquired you

edits.old: but unsuccessfully, for they were dealing with savage men
edits.new: but it was different, for they were dealing with savage men

fixed: The first problem was real: 'associating with' missed the sense of συνεῖναι as being with/cohabiting, and the suggested fix 'toward' better captures the relationship while keeping 'conscience' intact.
The second problem was real: 'but unsuccessfully' mistranslated ἄλλως μέντοι, which means 'but otherwise/in a different way,' so I changed it to 'but it was different.'

problems.quote: refusing even to perform the deed so called by name
problems.source_quote: μηδὲ τὸ λεγόμενον ὀνόματι πρᾶγμα χρᾶναι βουληθείς
problems.why: βουληθείς is aorist participle 'having wished/willing,' not 'refusing'; negation + βουληθείς = 'not even wishing to use.'
problems.fix: not even willing to do the thing called by name
problems.ruling: βουληθείς = 'having wished,' not 'refusing'; μηδὲ...βουληθείς = 'not even wishing to use,' not 'refusing to perform.'

edits.old: refusing even to perform the deed so called by name
edits.new: not even willing to perform the deed so called by name

fixed: The mistranslation of βουληθείς as 'refusing' is real; corrected to 'not even willing'.

problems.quote: a man who was a eunuch
problems.why: Four different terms for Potiphar; reader may not connect them.

variants.text: a man who was a eunuch
the one who had acquired you

problems.quote: not even willing to perform the deed so called by name
problems.why: Garbled circumlocution for adultery; reader cannot tell what 'the deed' is.
problems.fix: Render as 'the act called adultery by name.'

edits.old: not even willing to perform the deed so called by name
edits.new: not even willing to perform the act called adultery by name

fixed: The glossary issue about 'a man who was a eunuch' does not appear in the current English text; the English already uses 'the one who had acquired you' consistently, so no edit is needed.
The mistranslation is fixed by rendering the circumlocution as 'the act called adultery by name'.

last_rejected.quote: the one who had acquired you
last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'master' for δεσπότην; 'acquired' obscures relationship.
last_rejected.ruling: κτησαμένω means 'acquired'; no δεσπότην here. Glossary claim misidentifies the source word.

last_rejected.quote: perform the deed so called by name
last_rejected.why: Greek means 'use the thing called by name' i.e. commit adultery; 'perform the deed' misses sexual sense.
last_rejected.fix: not even willing to do the thing called by name
last_rejected.ruling: χρᾶναι means 'use'; 'perform the deed' conveys the euphemistic sense adequately within normal range.

last_rejected.why: Indicative, not question with 'were you managing'; rhetorical question expects 'yes'.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐταμίευου is indicative; 'were you managing' correctly renders it as a rhetorical question expecting affirmation.

last_rejected.why: Participial construction shows result, not alternative choice; 'instead' adds contrast absent in Greek.
last_rejected.fix: and defended the natural law in yourself
last_rejected.ruling: δέ marks contrast; 'instead' reasonably renders the adversative. Result vs. alternative is interpretive preference.

last_rejected.quote: Reuben and Judah gave the best advice—but it was different, for they were dealing with savage men.
last_rejected.source_quote: Ῥουβὴν καὶ Ἰούδας ἄριστα συνεβουλευσάτην, ἄλλως μέντοι, πρὸς ἄνδρας γὰρ εἶχον ἀνημέρους.
last_rejected.why: English hides that Eustathius addresses Joseph directly; 'gave' not 'gave to you' loses vocative force.
last_rejected.fix: Reuben and Judah advised you most excellently—but differently, for they had savage men to deal with.
last_rejected.ruling: No vocative in this sentence; 'gave the best advice' faithfully renders συνεβουλεύσατην. Direct address is contextual, not lost.
